newsitem.title: USA: USDA suspends Epitope in strawberry case.
newsitem.headline: USDA suspends Epitope in strawberry case.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said Thursday it suspended a California subsidiary of Epitope Inc from the agency's school lunch program for lying to the government about the source of contaminated strawberries.
The decision by the USDA also means Andrew and Williamson Sales Co is suspended from doing business with any other agency of the U.S. government, a USDA spokesman said.

"USDA is charging that Andrew and Williamson of San Diego, California, and its former president, Fred Williamson, falsely certified strawberries provided under contract for the School Lunch Program as '100 percent grown and packed in the United States,'" the USDA said in a statement.
The strawberries processed by A&W were linked earlier this month to an outbreak of hepatitis A in Michigan.
A&W's parent company, Epitope Inc, admitted in a statement on April 1 that the unit haed "inaccurately described" the berries as being domestically grown, when in fact they came from Mexico.

USDA, the Food and Drug Administration, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and the Justice Department are investigating A&W and its former president on possible criminal charges. It is not clear how soon that investigation may be concluded, the USDA spokesman said.
Mary Ann Keeffe, an acting under-secretary at USDA, said A&W and its former president would be suspended until the investigation is completed.
"Selling foreign produce to the School Lunch Program under the pretense that it was grown in the United States is a very serious violation," Keeffe said.
